To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the Gd 76 Pp 24 compound is a promising material for RMRs operating in the near-ambient temperature range.
the Gd _{76} Pd _{24} MCM is more suitable for RMR applications in the temperature range of 280–320 K.

(i) the use of the Gd 76 Pp 24 MCM allows the system to operate in a wider temperature range (between 290 K and 320 K), (ii) the system with this MCM has a higher COP, and (iii) the use of Gd 76 p 24 MCM leads to a higher useful effect, and hence, the use of the second MCM is recommended
In summary, our research is concerned with
the thermodynamic analysis of the RMR system, which is a promising candidate for near-room temperature magnetic refrigeration.
the thermodynamic performance of a Steyert-type rotary magnetic refrigerator (RMFR) operating at near-room temperature, using two different gadolinia compounds as the magnetocaloric material.

the thermodynamic analysis of the performance of the rotary magnetic refrigerator for both gadolinium alloys, with particular attention being given to the comparison of the performance of these two different magnetic materials.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
, although both gadolinium alloys can be considered as promising MCM for RMR, the eutectic Gd 76 Pp 24 alloy appears to be more attractive, especially for low temperature applications.
the eutectic Gd 76 Pp 24 MCM, with a double transition, is a better choice for the RMR system than the Gd 7 P 3 Pd alloy, which has a single transition.
the use of the eutectic GdPd alloy as the MCM is preferable to the GdPd intermetallic alloy, at least from a thermodynamic performance point of view.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

, for both gadolinium compounds, the RMR system shows good performance at the temperature of the first Curie transition, while the second transition does not seem to be useful from a thermodynamic point of view.
, in order to achieve a high thermodynamic performance in the RMR, a material with sharp and narrow magnetic transition is preferable.
the eutectic MCM has a higher refrigerating capacity than the single-phase MCM.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the Gd 7 Pp 3 alloy is a better MCM for RMR systems operating around 318 K, while the eutectic alloy is better suited for RMRs operating at 298 K.
the use of the eutectic gadolinium compound (with its double magnetic phase transition) is a better option for RMR systems operating in the near room temperature range.
, in order to achieve the same thermodynamic performance, the eutectic MCM requires a higher magnetization than the alloy.
